IND.about: India fills most of South Asia, running from the snowy Himalayas in the north to tropical beaches in the south, and includes the Andaman, Nicobar and Lakshadweep islands. It is the world's most populous country, home to ancient temples, the Taj Mahal and hundreds of languages. Its food, festivals like Diwali and Holi, and film industry are loved worldwide. Tigers, elephants and snow leopards all live within its borders.

standout.text: The Statue of Unity in Gujarat, 182 m tall, is the world's tallest statue.

BRA.about: Brazil covers almost half of South America, from the Amazon rainforest in the north to wide grasslands and long Atlantic beaches in the south. It is famous for football, samba and the Carnival in Rio de Janeiro. Most Brazilians speak Portuguese, which makes Brazil the largest Portuguese-speaking country. Its wetlands, the Pantanal, are among the best places on Earth to see jaguars in the wild.

standout.text: Brazil holds most of the Amazon, the world's largest tropical rainforest.

JPN.about: Japan is an island nation in East Asia, made up of four main islands and thousands of smaller ones. It mixes ancient temples and shrines with ultra-modern cities like Tokyo and Osaka. Its landscapes range from snowy northern mountains to subtropical beaches in Okinawa, and Mount Fuji is its best-known symbol. Japanese food, anime and bullet trains have fans all over the world.

standout.text: Japan opened the world's first high-speed railway, the Tōkaidō Shinkansen, in 1964.

NGA.about: Nigeria sits on West Africa's Gulf of Guinea, stretching from mangrove swamps on the coast to dry savanna in the north. It is Africa's most populous country, with more than 250 ethnic groups and hundreds of languages. Lagos is one of the continent's biggest and busiest cities. Nigerian music, especially Afrobeats, and its films are popular across Africa and far beyond.

standout.text: Nollywood is one of the world's largest film industries by number of films made each year.

FRA.about: France lies in Western Europe between the Atlantic, the English Channel and the Mediterranean, and also includes overseas regions in the Caribbean, South America and the Indian Ocean. It is known for Paris, the Alps, vineyards and castles along the Loire. French cooking, fashion and art have shaped tastes around the world. Every July, the Tour de France bike race loops around the country.

standout.text: The Louvre in Paris is the world's most visited art museum.

CAN.about: Canada covers the northern half of North America, from the Atlantic to the Pacific and up into the Arctic. Most Canadians live in a narrow band near the US border, leaving huge areas of forest, lakes and tundra almost empty. It is known for the Rocky Mountains, Niagara Falls and ice hockey. Polar bears roam the shores of Hudson Bay in the far north.

standout.text: Canada has more lakes than any other country, with over half of the world's large lakes.

AUS.about: Australia is both a country and a continent, set between the Indian and Pacific Oceans, and includes the island of Tasmania. Most people live along the coast, while the vast dry interior is known as the Outback. It is famous for Sydney's Opera House, Uluru and the Great Barrier Reef. Kangaroos, koalas and platypuses are found naturally nowhere else.

standout.text: The Great Barrier Reef is the world's largest coral reef system, visible from space.

EGY.about: Egypt sits in the northeast corner of Africa, with the Sinai Peninsula reaching into Asia. Almost all of it is desert, so nearly everyone lives along the green strip of the Nile and its delta. Ancient Egyptians built the pyramids, the Sphinx and the temples of Luxor thousands of years ago. The Suez Canal links the Mediterranean and Red Seas through Egypt.

standout.text: The Great Pyramid of Giza is the only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still standing.

river: Nile (one of the two longest rivers in the world)

MEX.about: Mexico lies between the United States and Central America, with coasts on both the Pacific and the Gulf of Mexico. Its land ranges from deserts in the north to volcanoes, rainforests and the Caribbean beaches of the Yucatán. Ancient Maya and Aztec cities still stand across the country. Mexican food, Day of the Dead celebrations and mariachi music are known worldwide.

standout.text: The Great Pyramid of Cholula is the world's largest pyramid by volume.

IDN.about: Indonesia is a chain of more than 17,000 islands strung between the Indian and Pacific Oceans, including Java, Sumatra, Bali and parts of Borneo and New Guinea. It has hundreds of ethnic groups and languages, united by the Indonesian language. Volcanoes, rice terraces and coral reefs shape its landscapes. Rare animals like orangutans and Komodo dragons live in its forests.

standout.text: Indonesia is the world's largest archipelago country.

ARG.about: Argentina stretches down the southern half of South America, from subtropical forests in the north to the icy tip of Tierra del Fuego. In between lie the high Andes, the grassy Pampas and the glaciers of Patagonia. Buenos Aires, its capital, is known for tango and grand old cafés. Argentine beef, football and dinosaur fossils are famous around the world.

standout.text: Aconcagua, at 6,961 m, is the highest mountain outside Asia.

KEN.about: Kenya lies on the equator in East Africa, with Indian Ocean beaches on one side and Lake Victoria on the other. The Great Rift Valley cuts through its middle, and Mount Kenya rises over the highlands. It is famous for safaris in parks like the Maasai Mara. Each year, huge herds of wildebeest and zebra cross its plains in the Great Migration.

standout.text: Over a million wildebeest pass through Kenya's Maasai Mara in one of the world's largest animal migrations.

CHL.about: Chile is a long, narrow country squeezed between the Andes and the Pacific along South America's western edge. Its north holds the Atacama Desert, its centre has vineyards and Santiago, and its south breaks into fjords, glaciers and Patagonia. It also owns remote Easter Island with its giant moai statues. Clear desert skies make Chile a world centre for astronomy.

standout.text: Chile's Atacama Desert hosts ALMA, one of the world's largest radio telescope arrays.

NOR.about: Norway runs along the western side of the Scandinavian Peninsula in northern Europe, with a coastline cut deep by fjords. It also governs the Arctic islands of Svalbard. Mountains, glaciers and northern lights draw visitors from around the world. Oil and gas made Norway one of the richest countries, and Norwegians are famous for cross-country skiing.

standout.text: The Lærdal Tunnel, 24.5 km long, is the world's longest road tunnel.

VAT.about: Vatican City is a tiny walled country inside the city of Rome, Italy. It is the home of the Pope and the centre of the Catholic Church. St Peter's Basilica and the Sistine Chapel, with Michelangelo's painted ceiling, are among its treasures. Fewer than a thousand people live there, but millions of visitors come every year.

standout.text: Vatican City is the only country whose entire territory is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

VAT.day: 8 May · Anniversary of the Pope's election

MCO.about: Monaco is a tiny city-state on the Mediterranean coast, surrounded on land by France. Its hillside streets, harbour full of yachts and famous casino in Monte Carlo attract visitors from around the world. The Grimaldi family has ruled it for over 700 years. Every spring, Formula 1 cars race through its narrow streets.

standout.text: The Monaco Grand Prix has raced through the city's own streets since 1929.

BTN.about: Bhutan is a small mountain kingdom in the eastern Himalayas, between India and China. Most of it is covered by forest, and its valleys are dotted with fortress-monasteries called dzongs. It limits tourism to protect its culture and nature. Bhutan is known for measuring success by its people's happiness, not just its wealth.

standout.text: Gangkhar Puensum, at 7,570 m, is the world's highest unclimbed mountain.

ISL.about: Iceland is an island in the North Atlantic, just south of the Arctic Circle. It sits on top of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, so volcanoes, geysers and hot springs are everywhere. Glaciers, black-sand beaches and waterfalls cover its landscape. In winter, the northern lights often dance across its long, dark skies.

standout.text: Vatnajökull is Europe's largest glacier by volume.

ZAF.about: South Africa is at the southern tip of Africa, where the Atlantic and Indian Oceans meet. Its land ranges from Table Mountain and the Cape winelands to dry Karoo plains and the savanna of Kruger National Park. It has 12 official languages and three capital cities. It is one of the best places in the world to see lions, elephants and rhinos.

standout.text: The Cradle of Humankind holds some of the world's richest finds of early human fossils.

DEU.about: Germany sits in the middle of Europe, from the North and Baltic Seas down to the Alps. Its cities, like Berlin, Munich and Hamburg, mix old castles and cathedrals with modern design. It is known for its cars, beer festivals and Christmas markets. Composers such as Bach and Beethoven were born here.

standout.text: Karl Benz built the first practical petrol-powered car in Germany in 1885.
